explanations.explanation: Yes, friend! Jesus gives the Twelve authority over unclean spirits (Mark 6:7). That's real power, and it's His to hand out. Twelve regular guys walk out the door with it, and I can't even get my mustache to hold a spatula straight.

I see why that one tempted you, since authority usually sounds like palace talk. But Mark 6:7 says Jesus gave them authority over unclean spirits. The text doesn't hand the Twelve any power over the rulers of Galilee. Their job is out on the road, not in a throne room.

Good guess, friend, since the Temple was a big deal. But the text never puts the priests in this picture at all. Mark 6:7 says Jesus gave the Twelve authority over unclean spirits. That's the power He sends them out with.

I get it, friend. Money feels like the first thing you'd pack. But Jesus tells them to take no money in their belts (Mark 6:8). The text says it plain, so the answer is False. I've seen folks pack more for a trip to the mailbox!
That's right, friend. Jesus tells them to take no bread, no bag and no money in their belts (Mark 6:8). So no money goes in those belts. A belt with no money in it is just a belt, I guess!
Yes! A staff is the one thing Jesus lets them take for the journey (Mark 6:8). Just one stick, and the rest of the gear stays home. That's what I call traveling light, friend.
A sword sounds like a serious travel buddy, I know. But Mark 6:8 says Jesus told them to take nothing but a staff. No sword shows up anywhere on this list. Just that one walking stick.
Makes sense, friend, since a lamp seems handy on a long road. But Mark 6:8 says nothing but a staff for the journey. The lamp stays home, and so does the bag it would've gone in.
Right, friend! Jesus says to wear sandals, but not a second tunic (Mark 6:9). That means one tunic each. What you're wearing is the whole wardrobe, and there's no outfit change at the next village.

Two feels reasonable, I know. One to wear and one to swap. But Mark 6:9 says sandals, but not a second tunic. So the answer is one. I've been in a drawer for years with fewer clothes than you'd think, and I survived.
Three tunics, friend? That's a suitcase waiting to happen! Mark 6:9 says they wear sandals, but not a second tunic. So it's just one, and not even a spare.

That's it, friend. Jesus says, "When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that area." (Mark 6:10). So they stay put in the house where they're welcomed. No hopping from door to door looking for a better offer!
I see the thinking, friend, since the Twelve do have a job. But Mark 6:10 says to stay there until they leave that area. The word is stay. Jesus doesn't tell them to work in that house.
Good guess, since they're traveling light. But Mark 6:10 says, "When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that area." The word is stay. Fasting doesn't come up in this verse.

explanations.answer: Shake the dust off their feet
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend! Jesus says, "…shake the dust off your feet when you leave that place…" (Mark 6:11). Notice the dust comes off when they leave that place. Dust, meet ground.
Whoa, friend, that escalated fast! Jesus never tells them that in Mark 6:11. He says to shake the dust off their feet when they leave that place, as a testimony against them.
I can see why you'd think that, friend. But Mark 6:11 doesn't say it here. Jesus says to shake the dust off their feet when they leave that place, as a testimony against them.
That's right, friend. Jesus says to shake the dust off, "…as a testimony against them." (Mark 6:11). The shake isn't a gift or a prayer. It's a testimony, and that's the word Jesus uses.
Fair guess, friend. But Mark 6:11 says to shake the dust off their feet "…as a testimony against them." It's a testimony, not a gift. Nobody's getting a bow on dust!
That's a thoughtful guess, friend. But Mark 6:11 says the shaking is "…as a testimony against them." The word is testimony. The verse doesn't call it a prayer.

explanations.answer: Drive out demons and heal the sick
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend! Mark 6:13 says they drove out many demons and healed many of the sick. Preaching wasn't all they did. Those hands were busy all over the road.

Building a synagogue in every town, friend? That's a lot of work for guys with one tunic each! Mark 6:13 says they drove out many demons and healed many of the sick. Nothing about building appears there.
Reasonable guess, friend. But Mark 6:13 says they drove out many demons and healed many of the sick. Collecting offerings isn't mentioned there.
Yes, friend! Mark 6:13 says they healed many of the sick, "…anointing them with oil." Oil is the detail the text gives. The passage doesn't say more about why, so I'll leave it there.
Water makes sense, since it's what most of us reach for first. But Mark 6:13 says they healed many of the sick, "…anointing them with oil." So it's oil. Water isn't part of the picture here.
Ashes are a fair guess, friend. But Mark 6:13 says they healed many of the sick, "…anointing them with oil." The word is oil. Ashes aren't in this verse.
